dedupe_keys.name: anwser asset network systemic risk model

description: ANWSER (asset network systemic risk model) quantifies the risk of financial contagion in a crisis, in which distress spreads through a heterogeneous interbank credit network and banks' shared investment portfolios. Each bank has a balance sheet of equity capital, interbank borrowings and deposits; a fall in the market prices of assets triggers losses, banks whose equity cannot absorb them fail, and failures propagate to creditors. The model's measure, the bankruptcy reproductive ratio, is the final number of bankruptcies divided by the initial number, and the paper derives an exact formula for two banks and simulates 500 banks to map how portfolio choices affect systemic robustness. It was written by Yoshiharu Maeno and Satoshi Morinaga of NEC, Kenji Nishiguchi of the Japan Research Institute and Hirokazu Matsushima, with version 2 posted on arXiv on 5 February 2013. Coverage is generic and synthetic. The paper is available free on arXiv; no code or data release is stated. Caveats: banks share one equity ratio, networks are stylised, and the model has not been calibrated to real banks in the paper read. For simulation it offers a simple network contagion model of how asset price shocks cascade through interbank lending, a building block for financial resilience studies. It is related to the DebtRank record in this catalogue, another interbank contagion method.
